summary.text: PLA blend is a PLA-based bio-blend of polylactic acid with a bio-copolyester. Makers sell it for prototypes, decorative models and some end-use parts, with a matte surface finish, and a maker recommends its own product for lower-temperature applications. On the H2C it prints at 190⁠–⁠230 °C, and most products need no heated chamber.

identityNote: Bio-based compounds whose makers' documents say they are PLA-based: Extrudr's safety data sheets, "based on PLA, contains copolyester" (GreenTEC; GreenTEC Pro in 2019, "bio-copolyester" in 2026), which purefil's GreenTEC Pro repeats; BigRep's for PRO HT, "Polylactic acid (PLA) compound"; 3DJake's own answer on niceBIO, "other contents besides the PLA"; and Spectrum, which files GreenyHT and GreenyPro under modified PLA. Named for that, by the owner's instruction (D106); made as "PLA family, polymer not stated". Polymers.csv's PLA blend row says only what a PLA base implies, with no density or melting point, and these products' Vicat (up to 160 °C) and heat deflection sit far from PLA's, so its printed state is not modelled and it is not estimated.

items.text: Its balanced performance and reasonable price make PRO HT a great all-around material, perfect for prototypes and some end-use parts such as custom auto interiors.
